specification.objective: Provide deterministic, bounded, read-only GitRex repository context through inspect, diff, show, compare, and change-context operations using shared typed application logic.

requirements.statement: Provide gitrex inspect with repository identity and root, exact HEAD and branch or detached state, configured upstream and ahead/behind counts, staged/unstaged/untracked paths, conflict state, local and remote-tracking branch metadata, and bounded recent history.

Provide inspect scopes minimal, change, branches, and full with deterministic documented contents; minimize path and history data in minimal scope, use full as the bounded default, and never fetch implicitly.

Provide gitrex diff for worktree, staged, base-ref, and from/to-ref comparisons; report changed paths and additions/deletions where available; support text patches and structured JSON metadata; bound output and explicitly report truncation.
Provide gitrex show <commit> with resolved full hash, parent hashes, author, timestamp, subject, body, changed-file metadata, and bounded patch output.
Provide read-only gitrex compare <left> <right> resolving both inputs to immutable commit OIDs and returning merge bases, left/right unique commit counts and bounded lists, and changed-file metadata.

Provide gitrex change-context --base <ref> combining resolved base and HEAD OIDs, merge-base and introduced commits, changed-file metadata, current staged/unstaged/untracked state, and conflicts by reusing shared inspect, diff, and compare operations.
Expose all new commands through the existing schema-v1 JSON envelope and deterministic capabilities list, preserve human-readable defaults, and retain existing CLI and TUI behavior.
All new operations are read-only, use local Git state only, and do not mutate refs, index, or worktree or perform network access.
Resolve user-supplied refs safely before passing immutable OIDs as Git revisions, and return stable structured CLI failures for invalid refs and repository state.
Bound large path, history, commit, and patch output with stable defaults and explicit truncation indicators; avoid buffering the complete patch in memory.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Inspect reports identity, root, HEAD/branch/detached state, upstream divergence, staged/unstaged/untracked paths, conflict state, refs, and bounded history in text and versioned JSON without fetching.
All four inspect scopes have documented deterministic field sets; minimal omits token-heavy lists and history, full is the bounded default, and scopes remain local-only.

Diff supports working-tree, staged, base-ref, and from/to-ref modes; reports changed-path status and available statistics; emits bounded text patches or structured JSON and clearly reports every truncation.
Show resolves a commit safely and returns its full identity, parents, author/date, subject/body, changed-file metadata, and bounded patch in text and versioned JSON.
Compare resolves both refs to OIDs and reports merge bases, exact ahead/behind counts, bounded unique commit lists, and changed paths in versioned JSON without side effects or network access.

Change-context resolves base and HEAD, reports merge base and introduced commits, changed-file metadata, uncommitted status and conflicts, reuses shared operations, and emits versioned JSON without network access.
Capabilities classifies inspect, diff, show, compare, and change-context as read-only and lists their supported output formats; existing human defaults and TUI workflows remain supported.

invariants.statement: Public JSON response DTOs remain independent from internal Git and domain representations and use the existing schema-v1 envelope.
Each supplied reference is resolved once to an immutable commit ID before it is used in a subsequent Git revision command.
All public lists are deterministically ordered and all truncated collections expose their full count and a truncation flag.
Read-only context commands never fetch, mutate refs, update the index, or modify worktree files.
Patch capture retains at most the configured byte limit plus a small detection buffer while draining the Git subprocess output.

forbidden_states.statement: A user-supplied ref is interpolated into a shell command or passed to Git as an option.
A patch or path list is silently truncated or an operation fetches to fill missing remote-tracking state.
New JSON output serializes internal structs directly or changes the existing schema version.
Inspect and change-context duplicate Git parsing or diff behavior instead of reusing shared operations.

inputs.statement: An invocation of inspect with an optional scope and bounded result limits.
A diff mode selecting worktree, staged, one base ref, or a from/to ref pair, plus optional output limits and format.
A commit-ish for show or two commit-ish references for compare.

outputs.statement: Deterministic text summaries and versioned JSON envelopes with explicit OIDs, counts, sorted records, and truncation metadata.
A bounded patch string for text output and optional JSON inclusion, with returned and total byte counts.
Stable error envelopes and nonzero exit codes for invalid repository state or references in JSON mode.

failure_semantics.statement: Invalid refs return the existing REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND protocol error before any dependent Git operation.
Git output parse and UTF-8 errors use the existing stable protocol codes and nonzero exit status.
A repository without HEAD can still be inspected; operations requiring a commit report a structured HEAD/reference failure.
Argument validation errors retain Clap's current usage-error behavior.
